technical_and_design_decisions: The software increment will be implemented as an extension of the existing Spring Framework/Spring XD codebase, adhering to its architecture and patterns.

For U1, U2, U3: We will implement a custom Spring Data repository backed by a Kafka changelog topic, using Apache Kafka Streams' interactive queries for off-heap state stores (U1) and a producer-interceptor or callback mechanism for acknowledgement-based flushing (U2, U3).
For U4: We will add a CoAP source module using the Eclipse Californium library, integrated with the existing Spring Integration or Spring Cloud Stream module architecture.
For U5: We will generate comprehensive documentation (e.g., AsciiDoc) covering all configurable properties for deployment, based on existing templates.
For U6: We will implement Kerberos authentication for Sqoop jobs by configuring the Hadoop security settings and providing a secure connection handler.
For U7: We will implement a Java client for the Diego Receptor REST API using Spring's RestTemplate or WebClient, with proper error handling and security.
For U8: We will complete the Boot-based ModuleRunner by finishing the deployment properties handling, likely involving configuration loading and lifecycle management in a Spring Boot context.
We assume a single developer will handle all tasks, with no parallel workstreams, affecting how activities are sequenced and estimated.
All estimates are for the core implementation work and include time for unit testing and basic integration testing within the existing test frameworks.
assumptions: The developer is familiar with the Spring ecosystem, Kafka, CoAP, Hadoop security, and the Diego receptor API.
Existing codebases (Spring XD, Spring Data) are available and accessible for modification.
No major architectural changes are required; the increment builds upon the existing framework capabilities.
Standard development tools and environments (IDE, build systems, test frameworks) are already set up.
There is no need for extensive research on the core technologies, as the developer has working knowledge.
Documentation (U5) will be written as part of the implementation, not as a separate phase.
Testing effort is included within each activity's estimate, with the assumption of writing unit tests for new code and performing manual integration tests where necessary.
The scope of each user story is limited to the described functionality, without additional feature creep.
We are working in a feature branch, and code reviews are assumed to be part of the overall process but not estimated separately.
